question: What is the correct points-per-rating conversion and the true residual SD of a game margin around a fair line?
what_we_have: The legacy board fit on n=33 rows gives beta=1.140, home intercept=-0.82 points and residual SD=11.92 points. A separate verified-track walk-forward evaluation on the 148-game corpus has 100 predictions: spread RMSE 12.58 versus 13.31 for a zero-margin baseline (gain +0.055, 95% CI [-0.020, +0.130]) and Brier skill +0.069 versus a coin (95% CI [-0.086, +0.229]). Both intervals include no improvement. This is not a sportsbook comparison and does not validate the legacy fit parameters.
what_we_need: Residual SD of (actual margin - model margin) on a full sample, and the same for totals
how_to_obtain: After Q-04, one OLS/robust regression; re-estimate each season and freeze before play
decision_it_unblocks: Calibration of the legacy spread/total probabilities; both 100-game walk-forward intervals span zero improvement, so no model-skill or betting-edge claim is established, especially without a licensed market reference.
source_gap: SRC-006 and SRC-007 link only to Weeks 1 and 2; the additional weekly URLs used by the separate 148-game corpus are not registered in data/sources.csv and are not cited by this row. The walk-forward evaluation covers one 2026 season; both its spread-RMSE-gain interval ([-0.020, +0.130]) and Brier-skill interval ([-0.086, +0.229]) include zero, and it does not establish a multi-season beta/residual-SD calibration or market edge.
